plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Bare, leafless flower stems push straight out of the soil. Each one opens into a goblet of delicate lilac-pink petals, like a crocus that has arrived early for the party. Whole meadows and borders look as if they have been scattered with pastel chalices just as other flowers fade.
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across Europe, and in temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The flowers appear in autumn, but the leaves emerge the following spring and die back by summer. The plant is also the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novi-belgii
plants.description: This tall, bushy perennial is covered in starry daisy-like flowers with sunny yellow centers and rays in shades of violet-blue. In autumn borders and roadside meadows it becomes a hum of activity as the last pollinators of the season crowd onto it.
plants.bloomingSeason: August through October, peaking in September
plants.location: Eastern North America, widely grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Late-season asters are a lifeline for migrating monarch butterflies. The butterflies refuel on the nectar before their long journey south.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Streets turn into tunnels of lavender-blue as the trees burst into bloom before most of their new leaves appear. The trumpet-shaped flowers carpet the pavements and parked cars below in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September through November in the Southern Hemisphere spring
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the tens of thousands of these South American trees lining its streets. Locals call the season of fallen purple petals a carpet of blossoms.
